name: point_at
description: Animate a large pointer onto one thing the user should click or look at. Use when telling the user *what to press next*. Prefer `kind: element` targets.

name: highlight
description: Mark something on screen. `spotlight` dims everything else; use it when the user asks where something is. `underline` for text. Use `tone: warning` for anything risky (suspicious links, delete buttons). Only one highlight at a time; a new one replaces the old.

name: label_parts
description: Point out SEVERAL parts of what is on screen at once (2-5): draws a ring and a short label on each, as one drawing. Use it when the user asks about the parts of something, what to look at, or why something looks suspicious (e.g. the sender, the link and the urgent wording of an email), and use `tone: warning` on the risky parts (default `info`). Prefer `kind: element` targets; use rects inside the user's selection when there are no element ids. Unlike `highlight` it does not replace the current highlight. For ONE thing use `highlight`.

name: show_steps
description: Show a short numbered path (max 5) across real on-screen controls, for multi-step tasks. Only the current step is emphasised. When the user will do the steps over several turns, pass `expires: 'on_target_selected'`: the guide then stays across turns until its last step is done (or you call `clear`); move it on with `advance_step`.

name: advance_step
description: Move a step guide forward when the user has done the current step.

name: show_explainer
description: Show a picture card beside something on screen, only when a picture explains better than words. `anatomy` labels parts of the user's own screen; `sequence` shows a short how-to; `compare` shows two things side by side (put the safe/correct one on the LEFT — it gets ✓ bullets — and the risky one on the RIGHT — it gets ⚠ bullets); `concept` illustrates an idea; `verdict` answers 'is this safe / real / a scam?' with a tone (`warning` for risky, `success` for fine, `info` if unsure), the card `title` as the headline (e.g. 'Likely a scam') and 1-3 short `reasons` (pair it with `label_parts` on the suspicious parts). Never put words inside `imagePrompt`; captions carry all text.

name: clear
description: Remove annotations. Call with `all` when the user says 'got it', 'okay' or changes topic.

name: move_avatar
description: Move the user's voice-assistant avatar bubble out of the way when it covers something you need to point at or show. `auto` picks the corner farthest from what is on screen; pass `avoid` to keep it clear of a specific target, or a corner name to choose one. Only works during a call. Usually unnecessary: the overlay moves the avatar by itself when a highlight or pointer would be under it.

name: magnify
description: Show a round magnifying lens (2x to 4x) over small text or a small icon so the user can read it. Use when something is too small to see.

name: replay_last
description: Show the most recent set of on-screen annotations again, when the user asks to see it again.
